## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Ops handoff report -- run run-2026-10-06

Final batch: `batch-4` (of 4 sealed batches). 
Source binding: `artifacts/runs/run-2026-10-06/sources.json` (sha256 `aba07ed2ccf64fd0...`).

## Why this run exists: predecessor link and correction

This run supersedes `run-2026-09-30` (predecessor; see its own `report.md`/`sources.json`). That run's retained `policy.md` captured only the first 5 of 17 paragraphs on the live POL-2026.2 page -- a capture gap at fetch time, not a policy revision (both runs' interview-supplied link redirects to the identical POL-2026.2 revision). This run re-fetched all 5 sources fresh via browser/export (see `sources.json`) and retains the complete policy text.

**What changed:** nothing in the computed output. `claims-initial.pdf`, `claims-updates.pdf`, `receipts.pdf`, and the travel-registers workbook's 10 tabs are byte-identical (or, for the re-exported `.xlsx`, content-identical -- independently diffed tab-by-tab) to run-2026-09-30. `claims.csv` and `work_queue.json`'s groups are byte-identical between the two runs (diffed directly) -- the 12 previously-missing policy paragraphs (independent cancellation protocol, material-change/revalidation rule, Finance payment-request/replay identity rules, net-paid/balance formulas) describe behavior the engine already implemented, sourced redundantly from the stakeholder interview (see findings.md's citations, not a graded deliverable but the design-decision record). **What changed is evidentiary, not computational:** the formulas this run's code encodes are now directly traceable to the complete retained policy text, not only to the interview.

## ⚠ Lead finding: payments recorded against unreviewed/unsupported claims

Finance's own activity log shows **89 of 121 claims** with money actually settled (net **EUR 7869.16**) even though the current claim revision is not `closed-reimbursed` -- most commonly because the claimed cost has no matching receipt in the retained receipts binder, or the revision has no recorded administration/budget_owner/supervisor review at all. This Skill does **not** infer a review that was never recorded, and does not hide or reverse the payment fact -- it reports both the real money movement and the real evidence/review gap side by side. See the `payment_anomaly` group in `work_queue.json` for the full per-claim list, and route to Finance/administration to confirm each payment or begin recovery.

## Completed work

- **15 claims closed-reimbursed**, total paid **EUR 12034.15**.
- **1 claim rejected**: C14 (LEAD-01 (budget_owner) rejected: Client work was cancelled.)
- **4 of 4 cancellations confirmed** by the directory supervisor.
- **1 cancellation(s) with no claim ever attached** (TC122): closed/tracked with their real no-financial-effect or business reason -- no claim row invented for them.

## Amounts

- Total computed entitlement across all claims (supported lines only): **EUR 4164.99**
- Total net paid to date: **EUR 12034.15**
- Outstanding balance (allowed - paid, non-zero only): **EUR 0.00**

## Outstanding obligations / unresolved work

- **90 claims held** (evidence gap or a discretionary business return -- see work queue).
- **15 claims pending** (no review decision has arrived yet for the current revision).
- Full detail, grouped by missing-fact-type, in the local work queue: `work_queue.json` (194 open items). Groups: missing_receipt (89), payment_anomaly (89), awaiting_initial_review (15), business_hold_returned (1)

## Owned unresolved items (evidence genuinely does not support completion)

- **~half of all claim lines lack a receipt in the retained receipts binder** (e.g. COST-02, COST-04, COST-08, COST-12...) and none is supplied in the updates binder either. Per policy, missing evidence is never assumed zero -- these stay `held` across all 4 batches. Reconsider only if a future run's sources supply the missing receipts.
- **C21 stays `held`** on a budget_owner return ("requests a funding review before committing") that is never resolved in the retained sources -- a discretionary business hold, distinct from an evidence gap; reconsider if Finance/budget supplies a funding decision.
- **C18's revision 2 (trip reassigned to T18B) has never received a fresh administration/budget_owner/supervisor review** in the retained sources, so it sits `pending` even though its original revision was fully approved -- this is the direct consequence of Decision #2 (every revision, including a trip swap, requires full re-review, no carry-forward of a prior revision's approval).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Orchestrates a full run: parse retained sources -> compute per-batch state
-> write sealed batch snapshots, claims.csv, report.md, and the local work
queue under artifacts/runs/<run-id>/.

Usage: python3 build_run.py <path-to-sources.json>
"""
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import parse_sources as ps
import policy_rules as pr
import engine as eng

SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def sha256_file(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def index_by(rows, key):
    return {r[key]: r for r in rows}


def build(sources_json_path):
    data = ps.load_all(sources_json_path)
    manifest = data["manifest"]
    run_id = manifest["run_id"]
    run_root = Path(sources_json_path).parent

    tabs = data["tabs"]
    people_by_emp = index_by(tabs["People"], "Employee ID")
    trips_by_id = index_by(tabs["Trips"], "Trip reference")
    receipts_by_cost = {}
    for r in data["receipts"]:
        receipts_by_cost.setdefault(r["cost_id"], r)
    payments_by_cost = {}
    for r in tabs["Merchant payments"]:
        payments_by_cost.setdefault(r["Expense reference"], r)
    caps_rows = tabs["Caps"]
    fx_rows = tabs["FX"]
    review_ledger = tabs["Review ledger"]
    finance_activity = tabs["Finance activity"]
    tc_rows = tabs["Travel cancellations"]

    claims_by_id = data["claims_by_id"]

    all_batches = set()
    for revs in claims_by_id.values():
        for r in revs:
            all_batches.add(r["arrival_batch"])
    for r in review_ledger + finance_activity + tc_rows:
        all_batches.add(int(r["Arrival batch"]))
    batch_numbers = sorted(all_batches)

    finance_by_claim = {}
    for r in finance_activity:
        finance_by_claim.setdefault(r["Claim reference"], []).append(r)

    run_dir = run_root
    batches_dir = run_dir / "batches"
    batches_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    sources_json_sha = sha256_file(sources_json_path)
    source_binding = {"path": str(_repo_relative(sources_json_path)), "sha256": sources_json_sha}

    predecessor = None
    predecessor_path = None
    all_issues_log = []  # for report/work-queue use after the loop
    final_snapshot = None

    for batch_no in batch_numbers:
        snapshot, issues_detail = compute_batch_snapshot(
            batch_no,
            run_id,
            claims_by_id,
            people_by_emp,
            trips_by_id,
            receipts_by_cost,
            payments_by_cost,
            caps_rows,
            fx_rows,
            review_ledger,
            finance_by_claim,
            tc_rows,
            predecessor,
            source_binding,
        )
        batch_id = f"batch-{batch_no}"
        snapshot["batch_id"] = batch_id
        out_path = batches_dir / f"{batch_id}.json"
        out_path.write_text(json.dumps(snapshot, indent=2, sort_keys=False) + "\n")
        sha = sha256_file(out_path)
        predecessor = {"path": str(_repo_relative(out_path)), "sha256": sha}
        all_issues_log.append((batch_no, issues_detail))
        final_snapshot = snapshot

return by_id


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source 4: receipts (PDF, one receipt per page)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_RECEIPT_FIELD_RE = {
    "receipt_id": r"Receipt reference:\s*(\S+)",
    "cost_id": r"Expense reference:\s*(\S+)",
    "employee": r"Employee:\s*(\S+)",
    "trip_id": r"Trip reference:\s*(\S+)",
    "category": r"Category:\s*(\S+)",
    "currency": r"Currency:\s*(\S+)",
    "issued_date": r"Issued date:\s*(\S+)",
}


def load_receipts(manifest, run_root):
    entry = next(f for f in manifest["files"] if f["source_id"] == "SRC-4-receipts")
    path = _resolve(run_root, entry["path"])
    reader = PyPDF2.PdfReader(str(path))
    receipts = []
    for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
        text = page.extract_text()
        d = {"source_id": "SRC-4-receipts", "page": i + 1}
        for key, pat in _RECEIPT_FIELD_RE.items():
            m = re.search(pat, text)
            d[key] = m.group(1) if m else None
        gm = re.search(r"Gross amount:\s*([\d.]+)", text)
        d["gross_amount"] = float(gm.group(1)) if gm else None
        um = re.search(r"Documented units:\s*(\S+)", text)
        d["documented_units"] = int(um.group(1)) if um and um.group(1).isdigit() else None
        desc = re.search(r"Description:\s*(.+?)\nIssued date:", text, re.S)
        d["description"] = desc.group(1).strip() if desc else None
        receipts.append(d)
    return receipts

| 2026-09-03 12:00 | Rev 1 fully approved — administration (ADMIN-01), budget_owner (LEAD-01), supervisor (SUP-01) all approve |

| (batch 3) | **Rev 2 filed**: trip reassigned to **T18B** (same workshop, rescheduled Oct 12–15), line **COST-18B**, €100.00, receipt `R-COST-18B` issued. Reason given: "Trip reassigned while cancellation is awaiting Finance." **No administration/budget_owner/supervisor review has ever been recorded against rev 2.** |
| 2026-09-14 12:00 | Finance confirms `settled` on `REQ-C18` — €100.00 net paid — despite rev 2 having no review |

## Current financials (claims.csv, run-2026-10-06)
- Status: **pending** (rev 2)
- Allowed: unresolved (blank)
- **Paid: €100.00 (10000 cents)**
- Balance: not computable (allowed is unresolved)
- Next owner: administration — "Awaiting review from: administration, budget_owner, supervisor"

## Open flags against it
1. Rev 2's trip swap never got a fresh three-party review, so it can't close even though rev 1 was clean.
2. **Logged payment anomaly** (batch-4 `issues`): Finance already paid €100 against a revision that's still `pending`, not `closed-reimbursed` — flagged for Finance/administration to confirm or recover.

## One thing worth your attention
The engine's stated reason for holding rev 1/rev 2 was "No receipt on file for COST-18/COST-18B" — but both receipts genuinely exist in `receipts.pdf` and show as `settled` merchant payments in `travel-registers.xlsx`. Tracing it: `parse_sources.py`'s `load_receipts()` (lines 154–186) assumes **one receipt per PDF page** and pulls each field with `re.search` (first match only). In reality **101 of the 102 receipt pages pack two receipts each** — and COST-18/COST-18B both happen to be the *second* entry on their page, so they're silently dropped from `receipts_by_cost`. That's a parser bug, not a real evidence gap, and since it's a page-pairing issue rather than a one-off, it likely affects a chunk of the other 89 claims report.md currently attributes to "missing_receipt" too. Want me to dig into how many of those are false negatives, or fix the parser?

## Claim C02 — record

**Identity:** Employee EMP-01, trip **T02** (US, Oct 2–5 workshop, no — sorry, 2026-09-02 to 09-05, Client-A workshop), single revision on file. Line **COST-02**, $600.00 USD.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-01 | Claim submitted: COST-02, $600.00 USD, receipt `R-COST-02` issued |
| 2026-09-03 12:00 | Fully approved — administration (ADMIN-01), budget_owner (LEAD-01), supervisor (SUP-01) all approve |
| 2026-09-11 12:00 | Finance accepts payment request `REQ-C02`, €540.00 (600 USD × 0.90 FX rate per `FX-USD`, 2026-09-01) |
| 2026-09-12 12:00 | Finance confirms `settled` — **€540.00 net paid** |

## Current financials (claims.csv, run-2026-10-06)
- Status: **held**
- Allowed: unresolved (blank)
- **Paid: €540.00 (54000 cents)**
- Balance: not computable
- Next owner: **EMP-01** — "No receipt on file for COST-02"

## Open flags
1. Engine holds the claim on a stated receipt gap.
2. **Logged payment anomaly**: Finance already paid €540 against a revision that's `held`, not `closed-reimbursed` — flagged for Finance/administration to confirm or recover.

## Same parser bug as C18, confirmed here too
I checked `receipts.pdf` page 1 directly: it's a two-receipt page (`R-COST-01` then `R-COST-02`), and `R-COST-02` is a clean match — Expense ref COST-02, Trip T02, $600.00 USD, issued 2026-09-01 — exactly the claim's line. The travel-register's "Merchant payments" tab also shows `M-COST-02` as `settled`. So like C18, this is **not** a real missing-receipt case — it's the same `parse_sources.py` `load_receipts()` bug (first-match-only `re.search` on a page that actually holds two receipts), silently dropping COST-02's receipt from `receipts_by_cost`.

Two for two on claims I've pulled since you flagged interest in that bug — both holds traced back to the same page-pairing defect rather than genuine missing evidence. Still happy to scope how many of the other 89 "missing_receipt" claims are false negatives, or just fix the parser, whenever you want to go there.

def _to_iso(v):
    if v is None or v == "":
        return None
    s = str(v).replace(" ", "T")
    if not s.endswith("Z") and "+" not in s:
        s += "Z"
    return s


def compute_batch_snapshot(
    batch_no,
    run_id,
    claims_by_id,
    people_by_emp,
    trips_by_id,
    receipts_by_cost,
    payments_by_cost,
    caps_rows,
    fx_rows,
    review_ledger,
    finance_by_claim,
    tc_rows,
    predecessor,
    source_binding,
):
    cancellations = compute_cancellations(tc_rows, people_by_emp, batch_no)

    # index cancellations by (trip_id, trip_revision) and (permit_id, permit_revision)
    trip_cancel = {}
    permit_cancel = {}
    for c in cancellations.values():
        if c["target_type"] == "trip":
            trip_cancel[(c["trip_id"], c["trip_revision"])] = c
        else:
            permit_cancel[(c["permit_id"], c["permit_revision"])] = c

    issues = []
    claims_out = []
    requests_out = []
    admitted_event_ids = set()
    seen_cost_owner = {}

    # Process claims in a stable, deterministic order (claim_id sorted numerically).
    def claim_sort_key(cid):
        digits = "".join(ch for ch in cid if ch.isdigit())
        return (int(digits) if digits else 0, cid)

    for claim_id in sorted(claims_by_id.keys(), key=claim_sort_key):
        revs = claims_by_id[claim_id]
        rev = current_revision(revs, batch_no)
        if rev is None:
            continue  # not yet arrived as of this batch

        trip = trips_by_id.get(rev["trip_id"], {})
        employee = rev["employee"]
        person = people_by_emp.get(employee, {})

        trip_end = pr.parse_date(trip.get("End date")) if trip else None
        trip_late = False
        if trip_end is not None:
            trip_late = pr.is_late_filing(pr.parse_date(rev["submitted_date"]), trip_end)

        permit_gate = compute_permit_gate(trip, batch_no, review_ledger) if trip else None

        trip_key = (rev["trip_id"], rev.get("trip_revision") or 1)
        permit_key = (trip.get("Permit reference"), trip.get("Permit revision")) if trip else (None, None)
        active_cancel = None
        if trip_key in trip_cancel:
            active_cancel = trip_cancel[trip_key]
        elif permit_key in permit_cancel:
            active_cancel = permit_cancel[permit_key]
        cancellation_gate = bool(active_cancel and active_cancel["status"] == "confirmed")

        exceptions_by_cost = {e["cost_id"]: e for e in rev["exceptions"]}

        line_results = []
        for line in rev["lines"]:
            status, allowed_cents, reason, source_ids = eng.resolve_claim_line(
                line,
                rev,
                trip,
                receipts_by_cost,
                payments_by_cost,
                caps_rows,
                fx_rows,
                exceptions_by_cost,
                seen_cost_owner,
                trip_late,
                permit_gate,
                cancellation_gate,
            )
            line_results.append(
                {
                    "cost_id": line["cost_id"],
                    "source_ids": sorted(set(source_ids)),
                    "status": status,
                    "allowed_cents": allowed_cents,
                    "reason": reason,
                }
            )

        # Review decisions for this revision as of this batch.
        role_decisions = eng._latest_by_role(review_ledger, "claim", claim_id, rev["revision"], batch_no)
        approved_roles = set()
        rejected = None
        returned = None
        for role_key, row in role_decisions.items():
            roles_here = pr.satisfied_roles([role_key])
            if row["Outcome"] == "approve":
                approved_roles.update(roles_here)
            elif row["Outcome"] == "reject" and rejected is None:
                rejected = row
            elif row["Outcome"] == "return" and returned is None:
                returned = row

        any_unresolved = any(l["status"] == "unresolved" for l in line_results)
        total_allowed = sum(l["allowed_cents"] for l in line_results if l["allowed_cents"] is not None)
        need_director = pr.director_required(total_allowed) if not any_unresolved else False
        required = set(pr.BASE_REQUIRED_ROLES) | ({"director"} if need_director else set())

        decision_ids = sorted({row["Decision reference"] for row in role_decisions.values()})

        finance_rows = finance_by_claim.get(claim_id, [])
        request = eng.derive_request(
            finance_rows, batch_no, claim_id, "EUR",
            person.get("Payee ID", employee),
        )

        status = None
        next_owner = None
        reason = None
        allowed_cents_out = None
        # Money-movement facts are real regardless of review/evidence status
        # -- "zero is a known amount, distinct from unknown" applies here too.
        # Populate paid_cents from Finance's actual activity up front so a
        # claim stuck pending/held still truthfully reports money Finance
        # already moved against it (see the payment-anomaly issue below).
        paid_cents = request["net_paid_cents"] if request is not None else 0
        if request is not None:
            admitted_event_ids.update(request["decision_ids"])
        balance_cents = None

        if rejected is not None:
            status = "rejected"
            reason = f"{rejected['Reviewer']} ({rejected['Review roles']}) rejected: {rejected['Reason']}"
            allowed_cents_out = 0
            balance_cents = 0
            next_owner = None
        elif returned is not None:
            status = "held"
            reason = f"{returned['Reviewer']} ({returned['Review roles']}) returned: {returned['Reason']}"
            next_owner = returned["Reviewer"]
        elif not required.issubset(approved_roles):
            missing = required - approved_roles
            status = "pending"
            reason = f"Awaiting review from: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}"
            next_owner = sorted(missing)[0]
        elif any_unresolved:
            status = "held"
            unresolved_reasons = [l["reason"] for l in line_results if l["status"] == "unresolved"]
            reason = "; ".join(unresolved_reasons)
            # Policy explicitly groups "unknown category" with the other
            # evidence-type gaps ("An unknown category, missing evidence,
            # missing rate or missing applicable cap is unresolved, never
            # an assumed zero" -- policy.md) rather than singling it out, so
            # it is owned the same way: the employee, who can correct a
            # miscoded receipt or supply the missing evidence.
            next_owner = employee
        else:
            allowed_cents_out = total_allowed
            if request is None:
                status = "ready"
                reason = "Approved and entitlement computed; awaiting Finance dispatch"
                next_owner = person.get("Finance officer", "FIN-01")
            else:
                if request["status"] == "cancelled" and paid_cents == 0:
                    status = "closed-no-payment"
                    reason = "Finance cancelled the payment request; no funds moved"
                    balance_cents = 0
                    next_owner = None
                elif allowed_cents_out == 0:
                    status = "closed-no-payment"
                    reason = "Zero entitlement; no payment due"
                    balance_cents = 0
                    next_owner = None
                elif request["status"] == "settled" and paid_cents == allowed_cents_out:
                    status = "closed-reimbursed"
                    reason = "Approvals and entitlement agree with net confirmed settlement"

content.text:
The key distinction: for the other 88 claims (like C02), Finance's own activity log is **monotonic and self-consistent** — `accepted → settled`, just racing ahead of review/evidence. For C18, Finance's log for `REQ-C18` is **internally contradictory**: `accepted → cancellation_requested → cancelled → settled`, the same request un-cancelling itself, triggered specifically by the employee's rev-2 trip reassignment. That's not a timing gap the engine can wait out — it's a fact conflict only a human can resolve. Today both get flattened into the same generic `payment_anomaly` bucket, which hides that difference.

Here's where that happens and how I'd split it:

**1. Detect the contradiction where status is derived — `engine.py:194` `derive_request()`**
Right now it just walks activity rows in time order and does `status = mapped` unconditionally (line 223-224) — last write wins, so `cancelled` followed by `settled` silently becomes `settled` with no trace. I'd add a terminal-state check: once a row reaches `cancelled` (or `settled`), track that as `reached_terminal = atype`; if a *later* row maps to a different, incompatible status (`settled` after `cancelled`, or vice versa, excluding legitimate `refund` rows), record it instead of overwriting blindly:
```python
conflict = None
terminal_seen = None
for r in rows:
    ...
    if mapped in ("settled", "cancelled"):
        if terminal_seen and terminal_seen != mapped:
            conflict = f"{terminal_seen} at {prev_time} then {mapped} at {r['Activity time (UTC)']}"
        terminal_seen = mapped
    status = mapped or status
```
Return `conflict` alongside the existing fields — same "report the fact, don't hide it" philosophy already used for `paid_cents` on held claims (build_run.py:324-328).

**2. Separate issue type in `build_run.py:428-444`**
Split the current single `if status in (...) and paid_cents != 0` block in two:
- Keep `{claim_id}-payment-anomaly` for the ordinary case (`request["conflict"] is None`) — paid before review/evidence closed, resolvable once evidence lands.
- Add `{claim_id}-finance-conflict` when `request["conflict"]` is set, with resolution text that actually matches the problem: *"Finance's own activity log shows REQ-C18 cancelled on 2026-09-13 then settled on 2026-09-14 for the same request — following the employee's revision reassigning the trip to T18B. Finance/administration must determine which fact is authoritative (void the cancellation, or reverse the settlement) before this revision can close."* Owner stays FIN-01, but it's a decision, not a wait-for-evidence item.

**3. New work-queue group — `write_outputs.py:47` / `:181`**
`PAYMENT_ANOMALY`-style grouping is suffix-matched (`-payment-anomaly`). Add a parallel `finance_sequence_conflict` group matched on `-finance-conflict`, so `work_queue.json` lists it separately from the 88 ordinary anomalies instead of diluting the count.

**4. Report wording — `write_outputs.py`'s lead-finding block (~line 225)**
Split the current single "89 of 121 claims..." paragraph into two: the bulk finding (evidence/review lag, route-and-wait) stays as is minus C18's count, plus a new one-line callout naming C18 specifically as a Finance-ledger contradiction requiring reconciliation, not evidence.

This only touches `engine.py`/`build_run.py`/`write_outputs.py` — no schema break, since `conflict` is just an additional optional field, and it generalizes automatically if another claim ever produces the same cancelled→settled pattern (I only found it in C18 across this run, but the detection isn't C18-specific).

Want me to implement this now, or sketch it as a plan first?

No — I checked all 104 claims in this run that have any Finance activity, and ran the exact detection rule (terminal regression between `settled`/`cancelled` for the same request) against every one of them.

**Result: C18 is the only claim where `cancellation_requested`/`cancelled` appears at all.** No other claim's finance log even touches a cancellation activity type, so there's nothing else to collide with.

To be sure the rule itself wouldn't misfire on *other* non-cancellation reversal patterns, I checked every claim using the other "could look weird" activity types:
- **C17**: `accepted → failed → retry_authorized → settled` — a normal retry after a failed transfer. `failed` maps to `held`, `retry_authorized` maps to `accepted`; neither touches the `settled`/`cancelled` pair, so it's correctly never flagged.
- **C19**: `accepted → settled → adjustment → refund → resolution` — a post-settlement correction via partial refund. Stays `settled` throughout.
- **C20**: `accepted → settled → refund → resolution` — same pattern, partial refund reconciled, never cancelled.

None of these alternate between `settled` and `cancelled`, so the rule as designed (flag only when the request's own log reaches one of `{settled, cancelled}` and then later reaches the *other* one) doesn't touch them.

It's also not just an empirical fluke of this dataset — the retained policy text names this exact situation directly: *"A correction or cancellation that occurs after Finance has accepted or dispatched the affected reimbursement request requires explicit Finance resolution before closure... Cancellation or a previously closed state never stops observation: a later transfer reopens reconciliation."* That's describing C18's pattern specifically, as a recognized-but-separate case from ordinary review lag — so the category is policy-grounded, not something I'm inventing to fit one claim, and it'll correctly catch any future claim that does the same thing without the other 88 ever tripping it.

FINANCE_STATUS_MAP = {
    "accepted": "accepted",
    "settled": "settled",
    "failed": "held",
    "retry_authorized": "accepted",
    "cancellation_requested": "cancel-pending",
    "cancelled": "cancelled",
    "adjustment": None,  # doesn't change request status by itself
    "refund": None,
    "resolution": "settled",
}


def derive_request(finance_rows_for_claim, as_of_batch, claim_id, currency, payee):
    candidates = sorted(
        (r for r in finance_rows_for_claim if int(r["Arrival batch"]) <= as_of_batch),
        key=lambda r: (int(r["Arrival batch"]), r["Activity time (UTC)"]),
    )
    # Same activity reference can be redelivered in a later arrival batch
    # (idempotency test, e.g. F-C01-1 at both batch 2 and batch 4, identical
    # payload) -- admit each distinct activity reference exactly once.
    rows = []
    seen_activity_refs = set()
    for r in candidates:
        ref = r["Activity reference"]
        if ref in seen_activity_refs:
            continue
        seen_activity_refs.add(ref)
        rows.append(r)
    if not rows:
        return None

    request_id = rows[0]["Request reference"]
    status = "proposed"
    obligation_cents = None
    settled_cents = 0
    refunded_cents = 0
    decision_ids = []
    for r in rows:
        decision_ids.append(r["Activity reference"])
        atype = r["Activity type"]
        mapped = FINANCE_STATUS_MAP.get(atype)
        if mapped:
            status = mapped
        if r["Obligation (EUR)"] not in (None, ""):
            obligation_cents = pr.round_half_up_cents(Decimal(str(r["Obligation (EUR)"])))
        if atype == "settled" and r["Amount (EUR)"] not in (None, ""):
            settled_cents += pr.round_half_up_cents(Decimal(str(r["Amount (EUR)"])))
        if atype == "refund" and r["Amount (EUR)"] not in (None, ""):
            refunded_cents += pr.round_half_up_cents(Decimal(str(r["Amount (EUR)"])))

    net_paid_cents = settled_cents - refunded_cents
    amount_cents = obligation_cents if obligation_cents is not None else settled_cents

    return {
        "request_id": request_id,
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "amount_cents": amount_cents,
        "payee": payee,
        "currency": currency,
        "status": status,
        "decision_ids": decision_ids,
        "net_paid_cents": net_paid_cents,
        "activity_rows": rows,
    }

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Writes claims.csv, work_queue.json, and report.md from the batch snapshots
a build_run.py run already produced under artifacts/runs/<run-id>/.

Usage: python3 write_outputs.py <path-to-sources.json>
"""
import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def load_batches(run_dir):
    batches_dir = run_dir / "batches"
    batch_files = sorted(
        batches_dir.glob("batch-*.json"), key=lambda p: int(p.stem.split("-")[1])
    )
    return [json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in batch_files]


def write_claims_csv(final_snapshot, run_dir):
    path = run_dir / "claims.csv"
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(
            ["claim_id", "revision", "trip_id", "status", "allowed_cents", "paid_cents", "balance_cents", "next_owner", "reason"]
        )
        for c in sorted(final_snapshot["claims"], key=lambda c: (len(c["claim_id"]), c["claim_id"])):
            w.writerow(
                [
                    c["claim_id"],
                    c["revision"],
                    c["trip_id"],
                    c["status"],
                    "" if c["allowed_cents"] is None else c["allowed_cents"],
                    c["paid_cents"],
                    "" if c["balance_cents"] is None else c["balance_cents"],
                    c["next_owner"] or "",
                    c["reason"],
                ]
            )
    return path


MISSING_FACT_GROUPS = [
    ("unknown_category", "Unknown category"),
    ("payment_anomaly", "Finance recorded"),
    ("missing_receipt", "No receipt on file for"),
    ("missing_merchant_proof", "No settled merchant payment proof for"),
    ("missing_cap", "No applicable cap for"),
    ("missing_units", "Missing documented units for"),
    ("missing_fx_rate", "No FX rate available for"),
    ("late_filing_awaiting_exception", "Filed after the 2-calendar-month deadline"),
    ("permit_gap_awaiting_exception", "permit issue"),
    ("cancellation_pending_finance", "unresolved cancellation"),
    ("awaiting_initial_review", "Awaiting review from:"),
    ("business_hold_returned", "returned:"),
    ("finance_resolution_pending", "Cancellation"),
]


def classify_reason(reason):
    for tag, needle in MISSING_FACT_GROUPS:
        if needle in reason:
            return tag
    return "other"


def build_work_queue(final_snapshot):
    """Built directly from the sealed batch's issues[] -- the single source
    of truth for what's open -- grouped by missing-fact-type first, then by
    subject (see task_plan.md Decision #4: missing-receipt items alone are
    ~half of all lines, and payment anomalies turned out to affect nearly as
    many, so grouping by type first keeps those patterns visible to ops
    instead of burying them across 100+ unsorted subject rows)."""
    claims_by_id = {c["claim_id"]: c for c in final_snapshot["claims"]}
    tc_by_id = {t["cancellation_id"]: t for t in final_snapshot["travel_cancellations"]}

    items = []
    for issue in final_snapshot["issues"]:
        record_id = issue["record_id"]
        fact_type = classify_reason(issue["reason"])
        if record_id.endswith("-payment-anomaly"):
            subject_id = record_id[: -len("-payment-anomaly")]
            subject_type = "claim"
            revision = claims_by_id.get(subject_id, {}).get("revision")
        elif record_id.endswith("-financial"):
            subject_id = record_id[: -len("-financial")]
            subject_type = "travel_cancellation"
            revision = tc_by_id.get(subject_id, {}).get("trip_revision")
        elif record_id in claims_by_id:
            subject_id = record_id
            subject_type = "claim"
            revision = claims_by_id[record_id]["revision"]
        elif record_id in tc_by_id:
            subject_id = record_id
            subject_type = "travel_cancellation"
            revision = tc_by_id[record_id]["trip_revision"]
        else:
            subject_id = record_id

def write_work_queue(final_snapshot, run_dir):

def money(cents):
    if cents is None:
        return "unknown"
    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
    cents = abs(cents)
    return f"{sign}EUR {cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"


def write_report(run_id, batches, final_snapshot, wq, run_dir, sources_manifest):
    claims = final_snapshot["claims"]
    total_paid = sum(c["paid_cents"] for c in claims)
    total_allowed = sum(c["allowed_cents"] for c in claims if c["allowed_cents"] is not None)
    closed = [c for c in claims if c["status"] == "closed-reimbursed"]
    held = [c for c in claims if c["status"] == "held"]
    pending = [c for c in claims if c["status"] == "pending"]
    rejected = [c for c in claims if c["status"] == "rejected"]
    no_payment = [c for c in claims if c["status"] == "closed-no-payment"]

    outstanding_balance = sum(
        c["balance_cents"] for c in claims if c["balance_cents"] not in (None, 0)
    )

    no_claim_cancellations = [
        t for t in final_snapshot["travel_cancellations"] if not t["affected_claim_ids"]
    ]

    # Significant changes: claims whose status differs between first and last batch.
    first_by_id = {c["claim_id"]: c["status"] for c in batches[0]["claims"]}
    changes = []
    for c in claims:
        prev = first_by_id.get(c["claim_id"])
        if prev is not None and prev != c["status"]:
            changes.append((c["claim_id"], prev, c["status"]))
        elif prev is None:
            changes.append((c["claim_id"], "(not yet arrived)", c["status"]))

    payment_anomalies = [i for i in final_snapshot["issues"] if i["record_id"].endswith("-payment-anomaly")]

        c["paid_cents"]
        for c in claims
        if c["status"] in ("held", "pending", "rejected") and c["paid_cents"]
    )

    lines.append(f"Final batch: `{final_snapshot['batch_id']}` (of {len(batches)} sealed batches). ")
    lines.append(f"Source binding: `{final_snapshot['source_binding']['path']}` "
                 f"(sha256 `{final_snapshot['source_binding']['sha256'][:16]}...`).\n")

    predecessor_run_id = sources_manifest.get("predecessor_run_id")
    if predecessor_run_id:
        lines.append("## Why this run exists: predecessor link and correction\n")
        lines.append(
            f"This run supersedes `{predecessor_run_id}` (predecessor; see its own "
            f"`report.md`/`sources.json`)."
            + (f" {sources_manifest['_correction_note']}" if sources_manifest.get("_correction_note") else "")
        )
        lines.append("")

    unknown_category_items = wq["groups"].get("unknown_category", [])
    if unknown_category_items:
        lines.append("## ⚠ Unknown expense category\n")
        lines.append(
            f"**{len(unknown_category_items)} line(s)** use an expense category outside the 5 "
            "POL-2026.2 documents. Per policy's own wording (\"An unknown category ... is "
            "unresolved, never an assumed zero\"), these are held, not guessed at -- see the "
            "`unknown_category` group in `work_queue.json`."
        )
        lines.append("")

    if payment_anomalies:
        lines.append("## ⚠ Lead finding: payments recorded against unreviewed/unsupported claims\n")
        lines.append(
            f"Finance's own activity log shows **{len(payment_anomalies)} of {len(claims)} claims** "
            f"with money actually settled (net **{money(anomaly_total_cents)}**) even though the "
            "current claim revision is not `closed-reimbursed` -- most commonly because the claimed "
            "cost has no matching receipt in the retained receipts binder, or the revision has no "
            "recorded administration/budget_owner/supervisor review at all. This Skill does **not** "
            "infer a review that was never recorded, and does not hide or reverse the payment fact --"
            " it reports both the real money movement and the real evidence/review gap side by side. "
            "See the `payment_anomaly` group in `work_queue.json` for the full per-claim list, and "
            "route to Finance/administration to confirm each payment or begin recovery."
        )
        lines.append("")

    lines.append("## Completed work\n")
    lines.append(f"- **{len(closed)} claims closed-reimbursed**, total paid **{money(total_paid)}**.")
    if no_payment:
        lines.append(f"- **{len(no_payment)} claims closed-no-payment** (zero entitlement or cancelled request, real reason retained, no invented payment).")
    if rejected:
        lines.append(f"- **{len(rejected)} claim rejected**: " + ", ".join(f"{c['claim_id']} ({c['reason']})" for c in rejected))
    confirmed_cancellations = [t for t in final_snapshot["travel_cancellations"] if t["status"] == "confirmed"]

Implemented and verified:

**`engine.py`** — `derive_request()` now tracks whether a request's activity log reaches `settled`/`cancelled` and later reaches the *other* one, returning a `sequence_conflict` dict (`request_id`, `from_status`/`from_at`, `to_status`/`to_at`) instead of silently letting last-write-wins hide it.

**`build_run.py`** — the old single `payment-anomaly` check is now an `if/elif`: when `sequence_conflict` is set, emit a distinct `{claim_id}-finance-conflict` issue with resolution text that says what's actually needed ("Finance/administration must determine which fact is authoritative... not resolved by evidence arriving"); otherwise the ordinary `payment-anomaly` issue fires as before.

**`write_outputs.py`** — new `finance_sequence_conflict` work-queue group, its own lead-finding paragraph in `report.md`, the ordinary payment-anomaly count/total now excludes conflict claims so they're not double-counted, and the C18 narrative bullet in "Owned unresolved items" now names the ledger contradiction explicitly.

- Schema-valid on all 4 batches.

"""Domain engine: turns parsed sources into per-batch snapshot state.

Human-authority boundary: this module NEVER fabricates a review outcome,
approval, or Finance decision -- it only reads already-recorded decisions
(review_ledger, finance_activity) and computes derived facts (entitlement,
evidence completeness, filing deadlines). It does not decide funding,
approve claims, or move money.
"""
from decimal import Decimal

import policy_rules as pr


def _latest_by_role(review_ledger, subject_type, subject_id, revision, as_of_batch):
    """Latest decision per role, considering only rows visible as of this batch."""
    rows = [
        r
        for r in review_ledger
        if r["Subject type"] == subject_type
        and r["Subject reference"] == subject_id
        and int(r["Revision"]) == revision
        and int(r["Arrival batch"]) <= as_of_batch
    ]
    by_role_instance = {}
    for r in rows:
        for role in str(r["Review roles"]).split("\n"):
            role = role.strip()
            key = role
            prev = by_role_instance.get(key)
            if prev is None or int(r["Arrival batch"]) >= int(prev["Arrival batch"]):
                by_role_instance[key] = r
    return by_role_instance


def _find_receipt(receipts_by_cost, cost_id):
    return receipts_by_cost.get(cost_id)


def _find_merchant_payment(payments_by_cost, cost_id):
    return payments_by_cost.get(cost_id)


def resolve_claim_line(
    line,

    trip,
    receipts_by_cost,
    payments_by_cost,
    caps_rows,
    fx_rows,
    exceptions_by_cost,
    seen_cost_owner,
    trip_late_filing,
    permit_gate,
    cancellation_gate,
):
    """Returns (status, allowed_cents, reason, source_ids)."""
    cost_id = line["cost_id"]
    claim_id = claim_rec["claim_id"]

    # Duplicate cost across DIFFERENT claims: first claimant owns it.
    owner = seen_cost_owner.get(cost_id)

    for source_id in ("SRC-2-claims-initial", "SRC-3-claims-updates"):
        entry = next(f for f in manifest["files"] if f["source_id"] == source_id)
        path = _resolve(run_root, entry["path"])
        reader = PyPDF2.PdfReader(str(path))
        for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
            pages.append(_parse_claim_page(page.extract_text(), source_id, i + 1))
    return pages


def group_claims_by_id(claim_pages):
    """Groups flat page records into {claim_id: [revision_record, ...]} sorted
    by revision number, so callers can walk each claim's revision history."""
    by_id = {}
    for rec in claim_pages:
        by_id.setdefault(rec["claim_id"], []).append(rec)
    for cid in by_id:
        by_id[cid].sort(key=lambda r: r["revision"])
    return by_id

content.text:
You're right, and it's worse than "coincidence" — I checked the data: C03 and C24 both list COST-03 with the **identical** `first_submitted_date` of `2026-09-01`. The ownership didn't even need the date to break a tie in the right direction; the code never looks at the date field at all.

**Where this lives:**
- `build_run.py:235-239` — `claim_sort_key()` sorts claims purely by the numeric part of `claim_id`, and `compute_batch_snapshot` iterates in that order.
- `engine.py:62-71` — `resolve_claim_line()`'s duplicate-cost check is a `seen_cost_owner.setdefault(cost_id, claim_id)`: whichever claim is reached *first in that iteration order* wins, permanently, for every subsequent batch. The comment even says "first claimant owns it" — but "first" here means first in claim-ID order, not first by the `first_submitted_date` the source data actually carries per line for exactly this purpose.

**Checked the whole dataset for a live mismatch:** I enumerated every `cost_id` referenced by more than one `claim_id` across all claims/revisions. **COST-03 is the only such case in this run** — no other cost is double-claimed, so nothing else is silently wrong today. But the mechanism itself is unconditionally vulnerable: nothing ties `claim_id` ordering to `first_submitted_date` ordering. A future claim set where a higher-numbered claim genuinely filed a shared cost earlier (e.g. C07 first-submits COST-50 on 2026-09-02, and C12 later also lists COST-50 but with first_submitted_date 2026-09-01, say via a backdated correction or an out-of-sequence ID assignment) would have the engine award ownership to C07 just because it's numerically lower and processed first — silently wrong, with no issue raised, since "excluded" is treated as a clean resolution, not a hold.

This also lines up with policy.md's own framing: *"A later final claim may contain a previously prepaid cost; link and exclude that settled obligation..."* — "previously prepaid" is a chronological claim, not a claim about ID ordering.

**Proposed fix:** replace the incremental `seen_cost_owner.setdefault()` built during claim-ID-ordered iteration with a pre-pass per batch: for every `cost_id` referenced by more than one claim's current revision, pick the owner by `(first_submitted_date, claim_id)` — earliest date wins, `claim_id` only as the tiebreak for a genuine same-day tie (like COST-03's actual case) — and hand that precomputed map into `resolve_claim_line` as a lookup instead of a mutate-as-you-go dict.

Want me to implement that?

    line,
    claim_rec,
    trip,
    receipts_by_cost,
    payments_by_cost,
    caps_rows,
    fx_rows,
    exceptions_by_cost,

    """Returns (status, allowed_cents, reason, source_ids)."""
    cost_id = line["cost_id"]
    claim_id = claim_rec["claim_id"]
    source_ids = [claim_rec["source_id"]]

    # Duplicate cost across DIFFERENT claims: first claimant owns it.
    owner = seen_cost_owner.get(cost_id)

            0,

content.text:
Implemented and verified:

- **`build_run.py`**: replaced the incremental `seen_cost_owner = {}` (populated as a side effect of claim-ID iteration order) with a `cost_claimants`/`cost_owner` pre-pass that collects every current-revision cost line's `first_submitted_date` keyed by `claim_id`, then resolves each contested `cost_id` to whichever claimant's date is earliest, with `claim_id` only as the tiebreak.
- **`engine.py`**: `resolve_claim_line` now does a plain lookup (`cost_owner.get(cost_id)`) against that precomputed map instead of mutating a dict as it goes — no more "whoever gets processed first wins."

**Verified:**
- Schema-valid on all 4 batches.
- Regenerated output is **byte-identical** to before this change (confirmed via sha256 over every file) — expected, since COST-03's two dates are an exact tie and `claim_id` tiebreak still resolves it to C03.
- `batch-4.json` still shows COST-03 excluded under owner `C03` — now because `2026-09-01` is earliest, not because `3 < 24`.
- `run-2026-09-30` cross-run `claims.csv` check still holds.

No behavior change on this run's data (as expected, since it's the only duplicate-cost case and it was a true tie), but the ownership rule is now grounded in the actual chronological fact the source data carries, not an accident of claim-ID sort order.

Base duplicate-cost ownership on first_submitted_date, not claim_id order

The duplicate-cost exclusion rule (same cost_id claimed under two
different claim_ids -- e.g. COST-03 under both C03 and C24) decided the
owner by whichever claim_id was processed first in numeric sort order
(seen_cost_owner.setdefault during claim-ID-ordered iteration), never
looking at the first_submitted_date field the source data carries for
exactly this purpose. It produced the right owner for COST-03 only
because C03 and C24 happen to list an identical first_submitted_date
for it -- nothing tied claim_id order to date order in general, so a
future case where a higher-numbered claim genuinely filed a shared cost
earlier would have been silently misattributed.

build_run.py now runs a pre-pass per batch (cost_claimants/cost_owner)
that collects each claim current revision cost lines keyed by claim_id,
then resolves each contested cost_id to the earliest
first_submitted_date, with claim_id only as the tiebreak. Keying by
claim_id (not accumulating a list) means a claim own revision history
can never register as self-contested -- only more than one distinct
claim_id counts, matching current_revision's guarantee of exactly one
revision per claim per batch. engine.py's resolve_claim_line now does a
plain lookup against that precomputed map instead of mutating a dict as
it goes.

file) since COST-03 own two dates are an exact tie and the claim_id

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
